Counsel for Applicant :- Avanish Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rahul Singh Dahiya
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Avanish Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rahul Singh Dahiya,
learned counsel for the informant, Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 1040 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B, 504 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Khurja Nagar, District-Bulandshahr, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu Rites on 10.05.2022 and subsequent to it, the applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected the victim to cruelty for demand of a Honda City Car as dowry, thereby leading her to death on 24.11.2023 at about 10:30 AM.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by more than one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

Learned counsel has stated that it is true that the applicant is husband of the deceased person, however, at the alleged time of consuming poison by the deceased person he was working in his factory which is in the same premise and when he got information about the incident, he rushed the deceased person to hospital.
There is no dying declaration of the deceased person, as such, it is a clear cut case of false implication.
The cause of death could not be ascertained, as such, Viscera was preserved and on chemical analysis of the Viscera, Organochloro Insecticide has been found in it.
The deceased was undergoing treatment through exorcism practices, which may have contributed to her mental distress and ultimately led to her committing suicide.
6. It is further argued by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 18.12.2023 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the applicant has not mentioned the clause about his criminal history and the deceased had expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant only.

It is also argued that the deceased was pregnant at the time of incident by about five months,
as such, the applicant is not entitled for bail.
8.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the delay in institution of FIR and there is no explanation to the said delay caused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant-Arun Gupta, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
